questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Availability - many spots in Poland

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not extremely easy, everything takes time in Poland.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a contact person. Very helpfull when she had the answers. A bit difficult when she hadnt

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Quite easy - we used Airbnb and had a good experience compared to some of our classmates who used offcampus student housing

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I dont think it is possibe to live on campus. Choose somewhere in/around centrum. Its nice to be able to walk everywhere. Warsaw is not as bike-friendly as Cph, so it is easiest to walk around (although public transportation is quite easy and very cheap!)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Even though i did not live there, i talked to severalpeople who had problems with bugs/bed bugs. They got no compensation and had to pay for somewhere to stay while the apartment/room got disinfected. It was the same stories from different housings

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register on the universitys webpage. The process is easy enough, although they have some rules about registering at other faculties that are a bit difficult to figure out

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: e-mails with instructions, although they were not too clear all of them - unless you just wanted to take courses at your own faculty

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the e-mails carefully

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The classes (most of them) are very unserious. It is just students doing presentations all the way through. It is hard to listen to, and you learn close to nothing: Students are just trying to read out loud what Chatgpt told them, in a language that is far more complicate than their english skills

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different! If you go there to learn i cannot recommend. If you want a chill semester with plenty of time to travel, it is definetely the place to go;)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Applied Criminology, Principles of Roman Lawa, European Legal Tradition, Legal Theory and Philosophy, Membership in the Eu and Global law classroom

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Principles of Roman law with Jakub Urbanik - he is a great teacher, and the only class i had that was interesting/motivational (almost also the only one where homework was required and you had to read)

Personal spending DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: nothing really

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: everything is a bit cheaper than here at home, although not as cheap as one might expect. All polish products are crazy cheap (potatoes, vodka, and everything else that grows in/is produced in Poland. The rest no so much

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: To really be a part of nonacademic opportunities i think it would be smart to live at some kind of studenthousing with others. The university is not to good at arranging, but ESN UW does quite a good job. They are the only ones tho, so activities might be a bit overcrowded.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The institution itself provides/offers nothing

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go join the Erasmus activities. Especially if you dont live at student housing. It can be difficult to meet people there.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel! there are many beautiful and underrated places in Poland. The nearby countries are probably worth a visit too

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not easy. The poles are quite closed off. The easiest way to meet people is to meet other exchange students

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: not really, especially not as  a non-smoker. Very few speaks english.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The whole culture is just very different from the danish. People say that we are closed off, but compared to Polish people i wouldnt say that we are.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Cheap public transport

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Student discounts is only available with a polish studentcard - be sure to get yours!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take the polish language course. I think that will ake some things a bit easier. Not everyone speaks english, especially not the older part of the population

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Knowing that you are able to navigate in a new and different country on your own

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting my exam dates. I even had my schedule for my next semester at home before someone could even tell me in which week the exams would be held...

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: not really

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
